entries.name: StableDomains
entries.description: Register, check, and renew domains and manage DNS over x402 — no accounts. Check availability/pricing, register (Route53-backed), renew, and edit DNS records (A/AAAA/CNAME/MX/TXT...).

usage.callShape: POST https://stabledomains.dev/api/register with JSON body {domain} (x402 USDC on Base, price $20-$150 varies by TLD/availability)
usage.outputShape: body.status ("active"), body.domain, body.nameservers[] (Route53 NS records), body.hostedZoneId, body.orderId, body.jobId
quirks: IRREVERSIBLE + EXPENSIVE: this actually registers a real domain on Route53 and charges $20-$150 USDC (price varies by TLD/availability). It is NOT a sandbox. Only call with explicit user approval and a domain they truly want.

Price exceeds the usual QA $6 cap. The qa-pay --cap was 25 (template default), so it paid $20 and registered masterkey-qa-test-20260608.com. confirmed=false/txHash=null in the qa-pay output but the registration response is a real active domain.
ALWAYS call POST /api/check {domain} first ($0.01-$0.05) to confirm available:true and read priceUsd/slotsRemaining before registering. Do not register an unavailable domain.
Body is minimal: just {"domain":"name.tld"}. No recipient/contact fields needed (Route53-backed, no accounts).

Post-registration management (status/DNS/transfer) uses separate SIWX-auth endpoints: GET /api/domain/status, POST /api/domain/dns, POST /api/domain/transfer-out (free, SIWX). Renewal is POST /api/domain/renew ($20-$150, x402).
Registry spec listed outward:false but this IS outward/irreversible — corrected to true.
usage.guide: Registers a real internet domain via Route53, paid per-call with x402 USDC on Base. First call POST /api/check with {"domain":"name.tld"} ($0.01-$0.05) to confirm available:true and read priceUsd (registration runs $20-$150). Then, only with explicit user approval (this is irreversible and expensive), POST /api/register with the same minimal body {"domain":"name.tld"}. On success you get HTTP 200 with body.status="active", body.nameservers[] (the Route53 NS records to set at any DNS host), body.hostedZoneId, and body.orderId. Manage the domain afterward via the free SIWX endpoints (/api/domain/status, /api/domain/dns).

quirks: Input is a query parameter (?domain=), not a JSON body — it is a GET. Pass the bare name or name.tld (e.g. 'mybrand' or 'mybrand.com').
Service checks a fixed set of common TLDs (.com .net .org .io .co .dev .app .ai .xyz .me) regardless of TLD supplied; read body.available_tlds / body.taken_tlds for the summary.
qa-pay reported confirmed:false / txHash:null but status 200 with full payload — settlement is async on Base; the call succeeded.
usage.guide: Call GET https://netintel-production-440c.up.railway.app/domain-availability/check with a ?domain= query param holding the brand name (e.g. ?domain=mybrand). Pays $0.002 USDC on Base via x402, returns 200 JSON synchronously. domain.description: Registrable domain to look up (e.g. stripe.com). ccTLDs without RDAP return 503 uncharged.
Domain name to look up (e.g. example.com)

usage.callShape: GET <url>?domain=<domain> — required query param `domain` (string, 3-253 chars). No request body. x402 payment on Base (USDC). For GET x402 use the MCP fetch path; qa-pay can fail to complete the x402 flow on GET.
usage.outputShape: DEFAULT (2s.io): data.ok, data.items[] (array, one entry per match), data.items[].domain, data.items[].ldhName, data.items[].handle, data.items[].registrar.{name,ianaId,url,abuseEmail,abusePhone}, data.items[].registeredAt, data.items[].expiresAt, data.items[].updatedAt, data.items[].statuses[] (camelCase ICANN EPP codes e.g. clientTransferProhibited), data.items[].nameservers[], data.items[].dnssecSigned, data.items[].rdapUrl, data.total, data.source.{provider,url,license}, meta.cost.usd, meta.settlement.{txHash,network,success}. ALT (hugen): undeclared.
quirks: FIELD-NAME / SHAPE TRAP: response shape is NOT uniform across the 3 gateways — code must branch on which backend served the call. 2s.io nests records under data.items[] (camelCase RDAP); netintel is flat snake_case (e.g. created_at vs registeredAt) and adds score/grade/findings; status codes differ (camelCase clientTransferProhibited on 2s.io vs lowercase phrase 'client transfer prohibited' on netintel).
2s.io: records are under body.data.items[] (NOT top-level); settlement metadata at body.data.meta? no — at body.meta.settlement (cost at body.meta.cost.usd).
GDPR: registrant personal data is redacted upstream and not returned by any backend.
2s.io: TLDs without RDAP return 404 TLD_NOT_SUPPORTED.

netintel: x402 v2 on Base, amount '1000' (=$0.001 USDC, 6 decimals), payTo 0xdaDc335482AD545296Fd7b28518A251fFCbEb9Df.
GET x402: qa-pay may return 402 empty-body/paid:false; verify via MCP fetch which completes payment and returns the body.

entries.name: Cloudflare
entries.description: Access the Cloudflare API (DNS records, zones, Workers, Pages, account resources) metered per call via an x402 pay-per-call gateway (HTTPay) at $0.002/call — no Cloudflare API token required.

usage.callShape: POST https://httpay.xyz/api/gateway/cloudflare/client/v4/zones with JSON body {name} — but REQUIRES an X-Upstream-Token header with a Cloudflare API token, which is not available under the keyless policy
usage.outputShape: body.error / body.instructions (401 auth-required error; no usable result produced)
quirks: Paid the x402 quote ($0.002 settled on Base) but got HTTP 401 in return — the HTTPay gateway charges first, then rejects without an upstream key (charge-then-fail).

The Cloudflare service on HTTPay is NOT keyless: it requires your own Cloudflare API token passed via the X-Upstream-Token header (authType: bearer). The registry description claiming 'no Cloudflare API token required' is wrong.
Error body lists accepted auth formats: bearer/token/bot/basic/apikey via X-Upstream-Token. None can be supplied under the no-API-key policy, so the endpoint is effectively dead for this registry.
usage.guide: Do not use. This HTTPay gateway endpoint takes the x402 payment ($0.002) and then returns HTTP 401 because the Cloudflare backend requires an upstream Cloudflare API token via the X-Upstream-Token header. There is no keyless way to call it, so any call wastes money. The registry's 'no token required' description is incorrect and this service should be dropped/pruned per the no-API-key policy.

entries.name: OttoAI DNS Lookup
entries.description: Resolve any domain in one call — A/AAAA, MX, NS, CNAME, SOA and TXT records plus parsed email-auth posture (SPF, DMARC, and detected DKIM selectors) — over DNS-over-HTTPS, returned as structured JSON.

domain.description: Domain name to resolve (e.g. github.com, stripe.com). Subdomains allowed.

usage.callShape: GET https://x402.ottoai.services/dns-lookup?domain=<domain> — keyless x402 (USDC on Base/Polygon/Solana, $0.001); result returned inline in the 200 JSON body (no polling).
usage.outputShape: JSON: { status, data: { domain, resolves, records:{ a, aaaa, cname, mx:[{exchange,priority}], ns[], soa, txt[] }, email:{ spf:{present,policy,record}, dmarc:{present,policy,record}, dkim:{selectorsFound[]} }, generatedAt }, meta:{ generatedAt, validUntil, stalenessSec, degraded, sourceHealth } }
usage.quirks: Resolved over DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) with redundant resolvers/failover. Returns email-auth posture (SPF/DMARC/DKIM) parsed from TXT, not just raw records. MX priority may be null. meta.validUntil gives a ~1h freshness window and meta.degraded flags resolver fallback. Accepts USDC on Base (eip155:8453, plain + permit2), Polygon (eip155:137, plain + permit2), and Solana.
usage.guide: Call GET with ?domain=<the domain to resolve>. No API key or account. Drop-in nslookup/dig replacement for agents: one call returns DNS records plus SPF/DMARC/DKIM email-authentication posture as structured JSON.

entries.name: NetIntel Bulk Domain Check
entries.description: Check availability of many domain names across multiple TLDs in a single call — submit up to 50 name/TLD combinations and get back per-domain registration status, registrar, and expiry concurrently, plus an aggregate brandability score and grade, so an agent can scan an entire naming shortlist in one request.

names.description: 1-50 domain names to check (alphanumeric + hyphens, 2-63 chars each), e.g. ["acme", "acmehq"]. Required.

tlds.description: TLDs to check, with or without leading dot (default: [".com",".net",".org",".io",".co"]). Total names x tlds must not exceed 50.

usage.callShape: POST https://netintel.dev/bulk-domain/check with a JSON body {"names":[...], "tlds":[...]}. names[] (required) is 1-50 bare domain names (no TLD); tlds[] (optional, default [.com,.net,.org,.io,.co]) is the TLDs to test each name against. names x tlds must total <= 50. x402 paid, no API key. Synchronous JSON result.
usage.outputShape: body.results[] (one entry per name x tld combination): .domain (full name.tld), .name, .tld, .available (bool), .status (registered|available|...), .registrar (string|null), .expires_at (ISO date|null), .days_until_expiry (number|null). Aggregates: body.total_checked, body.available_count, body.taken_count, body.names_available_all_tlds[] (names free on EVERY requested TLD), body.score (0-100 brandability), body.grade (letter), body.findings[] ({rule,deduction,detail}).
quirks: Input goes in the JSON POST body, not query params or path segments. names[] are BARE names (no TLD) — the TLDs are supplied separately in tlds[]; each name is combined with each TLD.
names x tlds must not exceed 50 combinations total, or the call is rejected.
If tlds[] is omitted it defaults to [.com,.net,.org,.io,.co]. TLDs may be given with or without the leading dot.
Provider caveat: when BOTH RDAP and DNS are unreachable for a name, its status falls back to 'available' — re-verify surprising 'available' results on premium/short names.
Results and aggregates are at the TOP LEVEL of the response body (results, score, grade, findings...), not nested under a data/output wrapper.
Same provider (NetIntel) also serves a cheaper single-domain GET check at /domain-availability/check ($0.002) — this bulk POST endpoint is the batch counterpart at $0.10/call.
usage.guide: POST to https://netintel.dev/bulk-domain/check a JSON body with names[] (1-50 bare brand names, no TLD, alphanumeric+hyphens) and optionally tlds[] (with or without leading dot; defaults to [.com,.net,.org,.io,.co]). Keep names x tlds <= 50 combinations. It is an x402 paid endpoint at $0.10 USDC on Base (also settleable in Solana USDC) — no API key or signup, the pay layer clears the 402. The response is synchronous JSON: iterate body.results[] for each name.tld combination ({domain, available, status, registrar, expires_at, days_until_expiry}); use body.names_available_all_tlds[] for names free on every requested TLD, body.available_count / body.taken_count / body.total_checked for a quick tally, and body.score + body.grade for an overall brandability read. Treat 'available' with caution on premium names (provider falls back to 'available' when both RDAP and DNS fail).

entries.name: NetIntel Certificate Transparency Lookup
entries.description: Query the crt.sh certificate transparency log database to enumerate every SSL/TLS certificate ever issued for a domain — returns discovered subdomains, certificate issuers, validity periods, wildcard/expiring/recently-issued certs, and a risk score flagging suspicious issuance patterns.

domain.description: Domain name to query certificate transparency logs for (e.g. example.com). Required.

include_subdomains.description: Whether to include subdomain certificates (default: true).

limit.description: Maximum number of certificates to return (default: 100, max: 500).

usage.callShape: GET https://netintel.dev/cert-transparency/lookup?domain=<domain>&include_subdomains=<bool>&limit=<n>. Inputs are QUERY PARAMS: domain (required, bare domain name), include_subdomains (optional, default true), limit (optional, default 100, max 500). x402 paid, no API key. Synchronous JSON result.
usage.outputShape: Top-level JSON: body.domain, body.total_certs_found (number), body.unique_subdomains[] (subdomains discovered across all certs' SANs), body.unique_subdomain_count, body.issuers[] (distinct CA names), body.wildcard_certs[] (wildcard common names found), body.expiring_within_30_days[], body.recently_issued[], body.certs[] (one per certificate: {id, common_name, issuer, not_before, not_after, sans[], is_wildcard, is_expired, days_until_expiry}), body.score (0-100 risk score), body.grade (letter A-F), body.findings[] ({rule, deduction, detail}).
quirks: Inputs go in the URL query string (domain, include_subdomains, limit), NOT the request body or a path segment.
Pass a bare registrable domain (e.g. example.com); include_subdomains defaults to true so certs covering subdomains are folded into unique_subdomains[].
Data is sourced from the crt.sh public certificate transparency logs; subdomains are inferred from the SANs of discovered certificates, so this doubles as a passive subdomain-enumeration tool.
Results and aggregates are at the TOP LEVEL of the response body (total_certs_found, certs, score, grade, findings...), not nested under a data/output wrapper.

The risk score is docked for wildcard certs and certs issued within the last 7 days (findings rules wildcard_cert_present / recently_issued_suspicious), so a low grade does not necessarily mean a real problem.
Failed calls are never charged (payment is only settled on HTTP < 400); the endpoint is SSRF-safe and blocks private/internal targets.
usage.guide: GET https://netintel.dev/cert-transparency/lookup with query params domain (required, e.g. example.com), include_subdomains (optional bool, default true), and limit (optional, default 100, max 500). It is an x402 paid endpoint at $0.01 USDC on Base (also settleable in Solana USDC) — no API key or signup, the pay layer clears the 402. The response is synchronous JSON: read body.unique_subdomains[] for passive subdomain discovery, body.issuers[] for which CAs have issued for the domain, body.certs[] for the full per-certificate detail (validity window, SANs, days_until_expiry, wildcard/expired flags), body.wildcard_certs[] and body.expiring_within_30_days[] for at-a-glance risk, and body.score/body.grade/body.findings[] for an overall certificate-hygiene read. Use it to map a domain's attack surface (subdomains), audit certificate issuance, or catch soon-to-expire or suspicious certs.

entries.name: NetIntel DNS Propagation Check
entries.description: Check whether a domain's DNS record has propagated globally by querying it across 10 geographically distributed public resolvers at once — returns each resolver's answer, the majority value, a propagation percentage, a consistency flag, and a readiness score so an agent can confirm a DNS change has fully rolled out.

domain.description: Domain name to check propagation for, e.g. example.com. Required.

record_type.description: DNS record type to query: A, AAAA, MX, TXT, CNAME, NS (default: A).

usage.callShape: GET https://netintel.dev/dns-propagation/check?domain=<domain>&record_type=<A|AAAA|MX|TXT|CNAME|NS>. Inputs are QUERY PARAMS: domain (required, bare domain name) and record_type (optional, default A). x402 paid, no API key. Synchronous JSON result.
usage.outputShape: Top-level JSON: body.domain, body.record_type, body.propagation_percentage (0-100), body.consistent (bool), body.majority_value[] (the record values the majority of resolvers returned), body.resolvers[] (one per resolver: {name, ip, status (success|timeout|...), records[], matches_majority (bool), response_time_ms (number|null)}), body.divergent_resolvers[] (names of resolvers whose answer differs from majority), body.score (0-100 readiness), body.grade (letter), body.findings[] ({rule, deduction, detail}).
quirks: Inputs go in the URL query string (domain, record_type), NOT the request body or a path segment.
record_type is optional and defaults to A; supported values are A, AAAA, MX, TXT, CNAME, NS.

Queries 10 fixed geographically distributed public resolvers (Google x2, Cloudflare x2, OpenDNS x2, Quad9, Comodo, Verisign, CleanBrowsing) concurrently; a resolver that times out shows status 'timeout' with empty records and lowers the score.
Results and aggregates are at the TOP LEVEL of the response body (propagation_percentage, resolvers, score, grade, findings...), not nested under a data/output wrapper.
Failed calls are never charged (payment is only settled on HTTP < 400); the endpoint is SSRF-safe and blocks private/internal targets.
usage.guide: GET https://netintel.dev/dns-propagation/check with query params domain (required, e.g. example.com) and record_type (optional, one of A/AAAA/MX/TXT/CNAME/NS, default A). It is an x402 paid endpoint at $0.03 USDC on Base (also settleable in Solana USDC) — no API key or signup, the pay layer clears the 402. The response is synchronous JSON: read body.propagation_percentage and body.consistent for a quick 'has it propagated everywhere?' answer, body.majority_value[] for the value most resolvers agree on, body.resolvers[] to see each of the 10 resolvers' actual answer and response time, body.divergent_resolvers[] for any that disagree, and body.score/body.grade for an overall readiness read. Use it to confirm a DNS change (A/CNAME/MX/etc.) has fully rolled out globally before cutting over.

entries.name: NetIntel DNSSEC Validate
entries.description: Validates a domain's DNSSEC configuration over DNS-over-HTTPS — checking DS records at the parent zone, DNSKEY records at the domain, RRSIG signatures, NSEC/NSEC3 proofs, and the validating resolver's AD bit — and returns a full chain-of-trust assessment with a readiness score (0-100) and letter grade.

domain.description: Domain name to validate DNSSEC for (e.g. example.com) — query param

usage.callShape: GET https://netintel.dev/dnssec/validate?domain=<domain> (x402, USDC on Base eip155:8453 OR Solana; no JSON body; domain is a required query param)
usage.outputShape: domain, dnssec_enabled, resolver_validated, chain_of_trust, components.{ds_record{present,count,algorithms[]}, dnskey_record{present,count,key_types[]}, rrsig_record{present,signatures_found}, nsec_or_nsec3{present,type}}, tld_ds_present, score, grade, findings[]
quirks: domain is a QUERY PARAM on a GET request (no JSON body): ?domain=<value>
This host (netintel.dev) advertises TWO accepts: Base USDC (eip155:8453) AND Solana USDC — paid cleanly on Base at $0.03
NetIntel does not charge on 4xx/5xx (input-validation, upstream, or server errors) per its agent fair-trade guarantee

usage.guide: Validates a domain's DNSSEC configuration over DNS-over-HTTPS — DS records at the parent zone, DNSKEY records at the domain, RRSIG signatures, NSEC/NSEC3 proofs, and the validating resolver's AD bit — returning a full chain-of-trust assessment with a readiness score (0-100) and letter grade. GET https://netintel.dev/dnssec/validate?domain=<domain> (x402, USDC on Base eip155:8453 OR Solana; no JSON body; domain is a required query param). Output: domain, dnssec_enabled, resolver_validated, chain_of_trust, components.{ds_record, dnskey_record, rrsig_record, nsec_or_nsec3}, tld_ds_present, score, grade, findings[].

entries.name: NetIntel Domain Age Check
entries.description: Determine a domain's age from registration data (RDAP, then port-43 WHOIS) with a Wayback archival-history fallback, returning creation date, age in years, first archive capture, a maturity signal, and a 0-100 trust score + grade so agents can flag freshly-registered domains used for fraud or phishing.

domain.description: Domain name to assess (e.g. example.com). Required query parameter.

usage.callShape: GET https://netintel.dev/domain-age/check?domain=<domain> (single required query param `domain`; no request body). x402 paid, no API key.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous top-level JSON object: .domain (echoed), .created_at (ISO date or null), .age_days (number or null), .age_years (number or null), .age_source ('rdap' | 'whois' | 'wayback_estimate' | null), .first_archived_at (ISO date or null), .archive_snapshot_estimate (number or null), .registration_to_archive_gap_days (number or null), .maturity (string, e.g. 'established'), .score (0-100 number), .grade (letter, e.g. 'A'), .findings[] (array, empty for clean domains). Result is at the top level (NOT nested under body.data).
quirks: Input is a query string param (?domain=), not a JSON body — it is a GET. Pass a full domain including TLD, e.g. example.com.

age_source tells you the provenance: 'rdap'/'whois' are authoritative registration dates; 'wayback_estimate' is derived from first archival capture when RDAP/WHOIS are unavailable (e.g. .io and TLDs without public RDAP); null means undetermined.
created_at, age_*, first_archived_at and gap fields can all come back null when the domain's age cannot be determined — handle nulls before computing on them.
Result fields sit at the top level of the response object, not under body.data.
This host (netintel.dev) advertises TWO accepts: Base USDC (eip155:8453) AND Solana USDC — paid cleanly on Base at $0.03.

qa-pay reported confirmed:false / txHash:null but status 200 with the full payload — Base settlement is async; the call succeeded and is billed only on success (NetIntel guarantees no charge on 4xx/5xx).
usage.guide: Call GET https://netintel.dev/domain-age/check with a single required query param `domain` set to a full domain name (e.g. ?domain=example.com). It is an x402 pay-per-call endpoint at $0.03 USDC on Base (also settleable in Solana USDC) — no API key, no signup; the pay layer handles the 402. The response is synchronous JSON at the top level: read .age_source to know the provenance (rdap/whois = authoritative registration date; wayback_estimate = derived from first archival capture for TLDs without public RDAP such as .io; null = undetermined), then .created_at / .age_years / .age_days for the age, .maturity for a coarse signal (e.g. 'established'), and .score (0-100) + .grade (letter) for the overall trust rating. Use .first_archived_at, .archive_snapshot_estimate and .registration_to_archive_gap_days as corroborating archival signals, and .findings[] for any flags. Use it to detect freshly-registered domains for fraud/phishing triage. Handle nulls — age fields are null when age cannot be determined. NetIntel guarantees failed calls (4xx/5xx) are never charged.

entries.name: NetIntel Domain Appraise
entries.description: Estimate the market-value tier of a domain name using transparent heuristics (length, TLD premium, dictionary-word presence, pronounceability, keyword value, numeric/hyphen penalties) and get back a 0-100 value/quality score, a value tier, a letter grade, and a per-factor breakdown — so agents can triage domain portfolios and prioritize acquisitions without a paid appraisal service.

domain.description: Domain name to appraise (e.g. pay.com). Required query parameter.

usage.callShape: GET https://netintel.dev/domain-appraise/estimate?domain=<domain> (single required query param `domain`; no request body). x402 paid, no API key.
usage.outputShape: Synchronous top-level JSON object: .domain (echoed), .name (SLD), .tld, .value_score (0-100 number), .value_tier (string, e.g. 'premium'), .factors[] (array of {factor,impact,detail} scoring contributions e.g. length/tld/dictionary_word/pronounceability/keyword_category), .characteristics{length,is_dictionary_word,has_hyphen,has_number,pronounceable}, .score (0-100 number), .grade (letter, e.g. 'A'), .findings[] (array, empty for clean names). Result is at the top level (NOT nested under body.data).
quirks: Input is a query string param (?domain=), not a JSON body — it is a GET. Pass a full domain including TLD, e.g. pay.com.
This is a heuristic appraisal (name length, TLD, dictionary-word, pronounceability, keyword value) — it returns a value tier and 0-100 quality/value score, NOT a dollar valuation or live sales comps.

Partial-failure design: signals evaluate concurrently; ones that fail are listed by name in .signals_unavailable[] (omitted from .signals) and .confidence becomes 'partial'. Per the provider, partial results never read as safe — factor .signals_unavailable / .confidence into any allow decision.

For a rejected candidate (all TLDs taken) the appraisal/typosquat/brand_collision sub-objects can be null and .verdict is 'avoid'; read .recommended for the single pick and each candidate's .verdict for the per-name call.

usage.outputShape: { ok: true, data: { domain, type, records: [{ name, ttl, data }], record_count, source } }
quirks: The query param is 'name' (not 'domain') and must be a fully-qualified domain, e.g. anthropic.com.
'type' defaults to MX; enum is A|AAAA|MX|TXT|NS|CNAME.
Pass check=email to get a combined MX+SPF+DMARC result with an email_ready boolean (useful before emailing/invoicing a contact) instead of raw records.
Records are resolved live via Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 DNS-over-HTTPS; results are cached ~5 min.
method enum also accepts HEAD/DELETE per the schema, but GET is the read call.
This is a different operation from Greeneris Domain RDAP (v1/domain/rdap), which returns authoritative registration facts, not live DNS records.
usage.guide: To resolve live DNS records for a domain, call ?name=<fqdn> with an optional type (default MX). Read data.records[] for the {name, ttl, data} entries and data.record_count for the total. For email deliverability/readiness use ?name=<fqdn>&check=email to get combined MX+SPF+DMARC. Each paid call is $0.002 in USDC on Base; the full result is returned inline in the 200 body.

entries.name: Strale Startup Domain Check
entries.description: Check whether a startup name/keyword is available as a domain (.com/.io/.ai/.co/.dev) and as a handle/package on Twitter/X, GitHub, npm, and PyPI — in one x402 call.

backends.inputSchema: GET query param: company_name (string, REQUIRED) — the company name or keyword to check. No request body.
backends.outputSchema: { keyword (string), domains[]: {domain, extension, available (bool), current_owner (string|null)}, social[]: {platform, handle|package, available (bool)}, available[]: {type, name}, taken[]: {type, name, details}, available_count (int), taken_count (int), best_available_domain (string|null), _meta: {capability, latency_ms, provenance:{source,fetched_at}, payment:{method,settlement_id,price_usd}} }

usage.callShape: GET https://api.strale.io/x402/startup-domain-check?company_name=<NAME> (company_name is a REQUIRED query-string param, not a JSON body; x402 USDC on Base)
usage.outputShape: Synchronous JSON. body.keyword echoes the name. body.domains[] lists each TLD (.com/.io/.ai/.co/.dev) with {domain, extension, available (bool), current_owner (null if free, else description e.g. 'Active website (HTTP 200)' / 'Domain registered but no active website')}. body.social[] covers Twitter/X, GitHub, npm, PyPI with {platform, handle|package, available}. body.available[] and body.taken[] are flat summaries ({type,name[,details]}), with body.available_count / body.taken_count and body.best_available_domain (string|null). Payment/latency meta under body._meta.payment and body._meta.provenance.
quirks: company_name is a query-string parameter, not a JSON body — it's a GET request; pass ?company_name=<name>.
Fixed price $0.054 USDC on Base (paid $0.054001, the exact maxAmountRequired '54001' / 1e6); openapi lists it as fixed mode.
Only checks a fixed set: domains .com/.io/.ai/.co/.dev and handles/packages on Twitter/X, GitHub, npm, PyPI — not arbitrary TLDs or other platforms.
best_available_domain is null when no checked TLD is free; available_count can be 0.
usage.guide: Send a GET to https://api.strale.io/x402/startup-domain-check with a single REQUIRED query param company_name (the startup name or keyword, e.g. acme) — no request body. It is an x402 paid endpoint, fixed $0.054 USDC on Base (asset 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, payTo 0x66D7C2F952362BFB24FD7F02a9beC9c754ea83bC); no API key. The response is synchronous JSON. Read body.domains[] for per-TLD availability (.com/.io/.ai/.co/.dev, each with available + current_owner) and body.social[] for Twitter/X, GitHub, npm, PyPI handle/package availability; body.available[]/body.taken[] give flat summaries with counts, and body.best_available_domain surfaces the top free domain (null if none). Verified 2026-08-07 with {company_name:'acme'} -> HTTP 200 (acme.co available; acme.com/.io/.ai/.dev + @acme/github/npm/pypi taken; best_available_domain=acme.co), $0.054001 charged (tx 0xa9098d1a02c8341516428ca70ff2dee1378df0e36fa00b1f11e2213ed54ee875).
